title: Formats: CSV, JSON, Parquet, Avro and ORC

videos.script: Fifty thousand bicycle rides, written five times over. {{five-files}} As CSV, they take almost three megabytes. As JSON Lines, more than eight. As Parquet, about one point three. {{sizes}} Nothing was compressed and nothing was thrown away. What changed is which values sit next to each other on the disk. {{layout}} Some formats keep a ride together, one field after another. Others keep a column together, every value of it in one run. {{rows-columns}} That single choice decides what is cheap: writing one event the moment it happens, or reading one column out of millions of rows. {{cheap}} This lesson opens all five. CSV has no types at all, and JSON has only a few. Parquet, Avro and ORC are binary, and each one carries its own schema inside the file. {{binary}} You will read the footer of a Parquet file and see what it knows about the rows. You will add a field to an Avro schema and still read last month's file. And you will watch a CSV give the wrong average without a single error. {{wrong-average}} By the end, you can choose a format for a job, and say why. {{end}}
